We need to simulate three experts collaborating, but final answer must be a single JUnit test file with markers. Provide test cases covering all public methods, edge cases, exceptions. Use JUnit 4 annotations @Test, @Before, etc. Need to import necessary classes from org.jsoup.nodes, etc. Since Attributes class uses other classes like Attribute, Document, Entities, etc. For tests we may need to create simple Attribute objects. The Attribute class is part of jsoup; we assume it exists. We'll need to test methods: get, getIgnoreCase, put(String,String), put(String,boolean), put(Attribute), remove, removeIgnoreCase, hasKey, hasKeyIgnoreCase, size, addAll, iterator, asList, dataset, html, toString, equals, hashCode, clone, normalize.

Edge cases: null key (should throw Validate.notNull -> likely IllegalArgumentException). Null value for put(String,String) allowed? It stores null and checkNotNull returns empty string for get. Also boolean attribute handling (null value). Removing non-existing key does nothing. dataset filtering only data- keys. html serialization with boolean attribute and other edge cases.

We need to test exception handling: html() catches IOException from html(Appendable, OutputSettings). That method may throw IOException only if Appendable throws; we can supply a Appendable that throws IOException to trigger SerializationException. However html() catches IOException and throws SerializationException. So test that.

We need to test clone returns deep copy (different arrays). Also equals and hashCode.

Implement test class AttributesTest with @RunWith(JUnit4) optional.

We'll need to create a dummy Appendable that throws IOException.

Also test normalize lowercases keys.

Edge case for putIgnoreCase internal method not public; but we can test via public put(String,boolean) which uses putIgnoreCase.

Test dataset returns map view that reflects changes.

Test iterator remove.

Ok.

Let's craft code.

We'll import org.jsoup.nodes.*; also java.util.*; import static org.junit.Assert.*;

Write test methods:

@Before public void setUp(){ attrs = new Attributes(); }

Test get non-existent returns empty string.

Test put and get.

Test getIgnoreCase case insensitivity.

Test put boolean true creates attribute with null value; getIgnoreCase returns empty string.

Test put boolean false removes attribute.

Test put(Attribute) sets parent.

Test remove case-sensitive.

Test removeIgnoreCase.

Test hasKey and hasKeyIgnoreCase.

Test size after adds and removes.

Test addAll merges.

Test iterator iteration and remove.

Test asList returns unmodifiable list (expect UnsupportedOperationException on add).

Test dataset: put data attribute via dataset.put, ensure appears, removal via iterator.

Test html: simple attribute with value containing special chars (e.g., "a\"b") and boolean attribute.

Test html exception: custom Appendable that throws IOException; call html(Appendable, settings) via reflection? html() private method? Actually html(Appendable, OutputSettings) is package-private? It's final void html(Appendable, Document.OutputSettings) with default visibility (no modifier) meaning package-private. Since test in same package org.jsoup.nodes, we can place test class in same package to access. We'll create test class in same package (package org.jsoup.nodes;). Then we can call attrs.html(appendable, new Document("").outputSettings()). Expect SerializationException.

Test toString equals html.

Test equals and hashCode: two attrs with same entries equal.

Test clone: modify original after clone does not affect clone.

Test normalize: keys become lower case.

Ok.
